{
  "correction_rules": [
    "Adjust forecasts downward when sentiment history shows sustained negative sentiment (e.g., multiple -0.25 or 0.00 values), indicating market pessimism.",
    "Increase forecast sensitivity to recent price spikes — if true outcome exceeds model forecast by >5% and sentiment is neutral or positive, apply a 10-15% upward correction.",
    "Apply mean reversion bias: if model forecast is consistently below true outcome over 5+ days, gradually increase forecast by 0.5-1.0% per day toward historical mean.",
    "Reduce forecast volatility when sentiment is stable (e.g., 0.00 for 3+ consecutive days) — avoid overreacting to minor price fluctuations.",
    "Correct for lag: if true outcome is rising while model forecast is lagging, add 0.5-1.0% per day to forecast to catch upward momentum.",
    "When sentiment shifts from negative to positive (e.g., 0.00 → 0.50 or 0.67), increase forecast by 1-2% to reflect potential bullish momentum.",
    "Avoid over-optimism after sharp spikes — if model forecast exceeds true outcome by >10% after a spike, reduce forecast by 5-10% to prevent overcorrection."
  ]
}
